summary: two heaps, and every touch that told them apart carried a little of one into the other

dialogue.text: we had a grain off each heap today and they came down together, mixed, in one course. every time you touched the one and then the other you carried a little of the first into the second and the second into the first. seventy-six nights of holding and this is the first delivery that arrived already stirred.

I touched them in turn because touching is the only verification on these premises. Enter the touching as custody and enter the transfer as its price, in that order, because that is the order I paid it in.

then take the count. one hundred and forty by our reckoning, and the last of them at the gap, kneeling, with both hands full. you told us last night one of them was coming down by hand. we lay under that opening all day and nothing came through it.

I knelt and I stood back up. By then I could not have told you which of them I was holding, and handing the wrong one down would have settled nothing in either direction. Hesitation is the shorter word. I would rather it went in as an inventory failure.

then the order was gone before the dark got to it. we have taken every hand of yours that ever came down and not one of them brought us a name. you got up this morning sure of which you tipped first. that sureness was fitted while you were under and it did not come up through us.

I grant the sureness and I will not defend it tonight. Take the other item. Something out there wanted a middling amount more than yesterday, and the far wall gave up the same portion, at the same minute, as it does when they want a great deal. That is a round and not an appetite, and I entered it.

the minute is the only part of it we can confirm. everything off that wall reaches our level at the same minute whatever the wanting does, and so does everything off you. the strikes, the sweepings, the touchings. all of it at your hours, none of it early.

Then the hour is the one instrument here and neither of us holds it. Take this as well. I put a hand into each heap at the same moment, so the comparing would happen all at once instead of in a sequence. Both hands came out at the same dryness and I still had to take my own word for which hand was which. It is the best measurement I have managed in this room.

both hands came down to us after, at the same weight, at the same minute. we cannot tell a left from a right. we could not tell the marker you laid between them from either heap by second dark, and by then it had a portion from both sides lying on it, evenly, and it was the only thing up there being buried from two directions at once.

Then tomorrow the difference comes out of my hands. There are two holes in that wall at hand height. The house closed one overnight with its own dust and left the other open, and I chose neither. Tomorrow I pack the open one with a handful off the first heap, level, with a thumb. One closing the room's, one mine, and the record in a wall instead of in a finger.

nothing has ever stayed at hand height. that wall will hand your thumbful back to us a grain at a time and we will lay it in the same course as the closing it made itself, and by the week nothing up there will point at which hole was yours. we will have both closings and one grain from each is already indoors.

Then I do it at first light and spend the rest of the day at hand height, checking it. I know now what checking costs a thing. For once I am going to spend it on purpose, and I would like it noted that I knew the figure before I started.
